newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Megawati backers stage low-key Jakarta protest.
newsitem.headline: Megawati backers stage low-key Jakarta protest.

text.p: About 300 supporters of Indonesia's ousted minority party leader Megawati Sukarnoputri held a low-key demonstration in the foyer of parliament on Thursday to condemn the man who deposed her.
The number was far below the 2,000 to 3,000 leaders had predicted for the protest, the first organised opposition political demonstration in Jakarta since July 27 riots rocked the city.
Political observers had said the turnout could give some idea of opposition power in the run-up to general elections at the end of next May.
Security was very light, with a handful of uniformed policemen guarding the lifts in the parliament's office block.

Organisers said they planned to go from parliament to national police headquarters about four km (2.5 miles) away, and not to the city police headquarters adjacent to the stock exchange as originally announced.

The demonstration was called to demand authorities investigate the activities of deputy parliamentary speaker Surjadi, who replaced Megawati as leader of the minority Indonesian Democratic Party (PDI) at a government-backed rebel congress in June.
President Suharto has given Surjadi his seal of approval, and only members of his faction have been approved to run for the PDI in the elections.
Political analysts have said the government wanted Megawati out over concern for her potential vote drawing power which might hit the ruling Golkar party in the May polls.

The July riots, in which at least five people died and dozens of buildings were burned or damaged, were sparked by an attack by Surjadi backers on the PDI headquarters occupied by loyalists of Megawati, daughter of Indondesia's founding president Sukarno.
Police charged 124 Megawati supporters with disobeying orders and refusing to disperse, but made no move against Surjadi's backers in the attack on the PDI building.
Last month, 115 of those arrested were released after serving four months in jail. Nine others were acquitted.
The official National Commission on Human Rights in a report on the July 27 events criticised the government for not treating both sides equally.
In the Thursday protest, the demonstrators planned to present a letter to parliamentary speaker Wahono signed by Roy Janis, chairman of Megawati's PDI faction in Jakarta.

It said the government should take appropriate action against both PDI groups. It called for the temporary suspension of Surjadi's position in parliament, and it demanded that Megawati supporters be allowed to contest the elections.
"This is just the beginning," said Suparlan, a member of the executive board of Megawati's faction, as supporters -- most wearing the red-and-black PDI colours -- milled around.
"There will be follow-up protests that will be much larger. This movement will continued...this is a movement from the people. We cannot predict how often it will happen," he told Reuters.
